subject.title: [Feature]: Separate external conversations from local agent sessions

question: Should OpenClaw introduce a durable core conversation-address contract, distinct from session keys, with owner-only agent tools and correlated inbound-reply interception?
rationale: Current main has reusable session-backed send and event primitives but no durable multi-peer identity, authorization, correlation, or transcript-ownership contract; those semantics affect core channel routing and cannot be chosen safely by an autonomous repair worker.

options.title: Add Unified Core Contract
options.body: Introduce opaque agent-owned conversation references and correlated turns while reusing existing Gateway send, channel ingress, and transcript primitives.

options.title: Extend MCP Only
options.body: Keep agent tools session-oriented and enhance the MCP bridge, leaving in-agent external coordination dependent on an MCP client and session route metadata.

options.title: Keep Raw Targets
options.body: Continue using the generic message tool and document transport identifiers, accepting manual discovery and request/reply correlation.

recommendation.title: Add Unified Core Contract
recommendation.body: Introduce opaque agent-owned conversation references and correlated turns while reusing existing Gateway send, channel ingress, and transcript primitives.

likelyOwner.reason: He proposed the exact contract, owns the product-direction decision, and has the strongest history on the closest existing channel-conversation implementation.
